newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka to publish quarterly GDP figures.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka to publish quarterly GDP figures.

text.p: Sri Lanka's Central Bank will begin publishing quarterly economic growth figures once a national statistical survey is completed in September, a Central Bank official said on Monday.
At present, the Central Bank publishes annual economic growth data, released in April.

The deputy director of economic research at the bank's statistics department, A. Karunasena, said the new data would give the government and companies a far more accurate picture of economic activity in Sri Lanka.
"Quarterly GDP (gross domestic product) figures will be available for each region of the country," he told Reuters.
"It will give details of income, expenditure, consumption and socio-economic background as well as unemployment figures," he said.
Another bank official said the figures would most likely be available on a quarterly basis in 1998.
"We are still processing the data and it will take us sometime to compile everything," said the official who declined to be identified.
The Central Bank has almost finished a year-long mini-census of a sample 9,000 households from urban and rural areas.

The survey, the bank's seventh since 1953, covers all areas of the island except a portion of the north and east where the government is fighting a bitter civil war with separatist Tamil Tiger guerrillas.
Official data have largely ignored the mainly rural war zone since the war began in the early 1980s.
Sri Lanka's 18.3 million people had a per capita GDP of $760 in 1996, according to the latest annual Central Bank survey.
